answers.question: Within how many minutes must a mine operator call MSHA after an accident that kills a miner?
answers.answer: A mine operator must immediately contact MSHA at once without delay, and in any case within 15 minutes, after a death occurs at the mine (and this same 15-minute requirement applies to other accidents listed in §50.10, including injuries with reasonable potential to cause death and entrapments with reasonable potential to cause death).

claims.text: The operator shall immediately contact MSHA within 15 minutes at the toll-free number once it knows an accident involving a death has occurred.
claims.quote: The operator shall immediately contact MSHA at once without delay and within 15 minutes at the toll-free number, 1-800-746-1553, once the operator knows or should know that an accident has occurred involving: (a) A death of an individual at the mine;

answers.question: What minimum incombustible content must the combined dust in an underground coal mine keep where no methane is present?
answers.answer: Where rock dust is required to be applied in an underground coal mine, it must be distributed and maintained so that the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust is not less than 80 percent. This 80 percent figure is the baseline requirement; it only needs to be increased when methane is present in the ventilating current (by 0.4 percent for each 0.1 percent of methane). So where no methane is present, the minimum required incombustible content of the combined dust remains 80 percent.

claims.text: Rock dust must be distributed and maintained so that the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust is not less than 80 percent.
claims.quote: it shall be distributed upon the top, floor, and sides of all underground areas of a coal mine and maintained in such quantities that the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust shall be not less than 80 percent.

claims.text: The incombustible content requirement is only increased above the base level when methane is present in the ventilating current, by 0.4 percent for each 0.1 percent of methane.
claims.quote: Where methane is present in any ventilating current, the percent of incombustible content of such combined dust shall be increased 0.4 percent for each 0.1 percent of methane.

answers.question: How long must the self-rescue device given to each underground coal miner be able to protect that person?
answers.answer: Each operator must make available to every miner who goes underground (and authorized visitors) an approved self-rescue device or devices adequate to protect that person for 1 hour or longer.

claims.text: Each operator shall make available to each miner who goes underground an approved self-rescue device adequate to protect such person for 1 hour or longer.
claims.quote: Each operator shall make available to each miner who goes underground, and to visitors authorized to enter the mine by the operator, an approved self-rescue device or devices which is adequate to protect such person for 1 hour or longer.

answers.question: How often must an underground metal or nonmetal mine hold evacuation drills?
answers.answer: At least once every six months, underground metal/nonmetal mines must hold mine evacuation drills to assess the ability of all persons underground to reach the surface or other designated points of safety within the time limits of the self-rescue devices that would be used during an actual emergency.

claims.text: Mine evacuation drills must be held at least once every six months to assess the ability of all persons underground to reach the surface or other designated points of safety within the time limits of the self-rescue devices that would be used during an actual emergency.
claims.quote: At least once every six months, mine evacuation drills shall be held to assess the ability of all persons underground to reach the surface or other designated points of safety within the time limits of the self-rescue devices that would be used during an actual emergency.

answers.question: How many hours of training must a new underground miner receive before being assigned to work duties?
answers.answer: A new underground miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties.

claims.text: Each new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training before such miner is assigned to work duties.
claims.quote: Each new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training as prescribed in this section before such miner is assigned to work duties.

claims.text: The training is to be conducted in conditions duplicating actual underground conditions, with about 8 hours given at the minesite.
claims.quote: Such training shall be conducted in conditions which as closely as practicable duplicate actual underground conditions, and approximately 8 hours of training shall be given at the minesite.

answers.question: What is the permissible exposure level for noise at a mine, as an 8-hour average?
answers.answer: Under MSHA's noise standard, the permissible exposure level (PEL) for noise is defined in terms of an 8-hour time-weighted average (TWA8) exposure. The mine operator must ensure no miner is exposed during any work shift to noise exceeding the PEL. A miner's noise dose (and the corresponding TWA8 reading) must be calculated using a 90-dB criterion level and a 5-dB exchange rate, with A-weighting and slow-response instrument settings, without any adjustment for hearing protector use. Regardless of controls or protection, no miner may ever be exposed to sound levels exceeding 115 dBA (unadjusted for hearing protectors).

claims.text: The mine operator must assure that no miner is exposed during any work shift to noise that exceeds the permissible exposure level.
claims.quote: The mine operator must assure that no miner is exposed during any work shift to noise that exceeds the permissible exposure level.

claims.text: No miner may be exposed at any time to sound levels exceeding 115 dBA, without adjustment for hearing protector use.
claims.quote: The mine operator must assure that no miner is exposed at any time to sound levels exceeding 115 dBA, as determined without adjustment for the use of any hearing protector.

claims.text: The mine operator must use Table 62-2 when converting from dose readings to equivalent TWA8 readings, showing the PEL is expressed as a TWA8.
claims.quote: The mine operator must use Table 62-2 when converting from dose readings to equivalent TWA8 readings.

claims.text: The noise dose determination (which underlies the TWA8/PEL) must use a 90-dB criterion level and a 5-dB exchange rate, with A-weighting and slow response settings, without adjustment for hearing protectors.
claims.quote: Be made without adjustment for the use of any hearing protector; (ii) Integrate all sound levels over the appropriate range; (iii) Reflect the miner's full work shift; (iv) Use a 90-dB criterion level and a 5-dB exchange rate; and (v) Use the A-weighting and slow response instrument settings.

answers.question: How high must berms or guardrails be on the banks of roadways at metal and nonmetal mines?
answers.answer: At metal and nonmetal mines, berms or guardrails must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment that usually travels the roadway. This requirement applies to both surface (30 CFR 56.9300) and underground (30 CFR 57.9300) metal and nonmetal mine standards, and berms may have openings as necessary for roadway drainage.

answers.question: For how many hours must the breathable air in an approved refuge alternative sustain each person?
answers.answer: The breathable air provided within an approved refuge alternative must sustain each person for 96 hours.
